extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedy/satire writers applying to The Onion Writing Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for applicants to The Onion six-month Writing Fellowship (in‑office, Chicago) including eligibility, responsibilities, required writing samples, and qualifications. Specifies exact sample formats and submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location & work arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be located in, or willing to relocate to, Chicago, IL for the duration of the Fellowship. This is a full-time, in-office position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to be physically present in Chicago for the six-month program and work full-time hours as staff writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and start
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship is a six-month-long intensive and esteemed program beginning Late August.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be available to begin in late August and commit to the full six-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication to Onion content
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are fully dedicated to writing Onion content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the Fellowship, participants focus on producing material for The Onion and related verticals rather than external projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of work / verticals
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may also produce written content across all verticals including but not limited to The Onion, Onion Sports, editorial video, features, and any special projects (books, live events, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to write in multiple formats and for different sections; the role includes varied assignments beyond headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities — writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline, features, and draft writing for prose and multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate ability to write strong headlines, feature pieces, drafts for prose, and scripts or copy for multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities — special projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Special projects by request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows will accept ad-hoc assignments such as books, live events, or other editorial projects as requested by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities — meeting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting participation — attend all required timely, issue picking, evergreen, sports, and read-through meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliably attending and contributing to editorial meetings is an expected part of the role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities — additional duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional duties as assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility to take on various editorial or production tasks beyond listed responsibilities is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with The Onion's style and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity with The Onion’s style and unique voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should know and be able to emulate The Onion's tone, satirical approach, and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing skills — headline, draft, feature, video script
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong headline, draft, feature, and video script writing skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable proficiency across multiple short- and long-form comedic formats is required; samples should show range and polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical aptitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Aptitude for thoughtfully satirizing cultural the zeitgeist and society at large
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should show capacity to craft satire that engages with current culture thoughtfully rather than relying on cheap jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and giving notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to identify weakness in others’ written pieces and give tactful notes to help them improve
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teamwork and constructive editorial feedback skills are important; applicants should be able to critique collaboratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in group-oriented idea generation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being an active contributor in group brainstorming sessions is a required aspect of the role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management & deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to work under and meet tight deadlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must demonstrate reliability producing quality material on short timelines common in news/satire publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication contingent on quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of a Fellow’s material is always contingent on quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a Fellow does not guarantee publication; submissions must meet editorial standards to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: $35,000, paid on a semi-monthly payroll schedule (or the equivalent to $70,000 per year). Full eligibility for our benefits offering, including Medical, Vision, Dental, Disability, and Life Insurance. (They fully cover the cost of our base medical insurance for the employee.) We also offer Unlimited PTO, in consultation with your Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary and benefits are specified; applicants should understand the stated pay structure and benefits package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of positions available
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two fellowship positions available this session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited openings — competition is for two slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In your Cover Letter, please include: A brief, one-paragraph cover letter touching on your experience and the diverse viewpoint you would bring to the position
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter should be concise (one paragraph) and explicitly mention relevant experience and the diverse perspective you offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing samples — submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing samples in a single PDF attachment as part of your cover letter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required samples must be combined into one PDF and attached with the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing samples — 15 Onion-style headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of exactly 15 Onion-style headlines (no copy, just headlines)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exactly 15 headline-only ideas; do not include body copy for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing samples — two News In Brief (NIB) articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Two (2) written-out News In Brief articles. Choose two headlines from your list of 15 and write them out in the traditional Onion NIB length and structure. Use short-form articles on theonion.com for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select two of your submitted headlines and expand them into full NIB-format short-form pieces matching The Onion's typical structure and length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing samples — one 1–2 page video script
rubrics_metrics.description: One (1) one- to two-page script for the one of the following videos: either “Ex-Pastor Explains How He Was Turned Off From Religion After Sexual Abuse Charges Were Brought Against Him” or “Expectant Mother Reveals Heartbreaking Moment Doctor Told Her Baby Wouldn’t Make It Big In Hollywood.” Scripts should be formatted like this example. Use Now: Focus videos on
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a 1–2 page script for one of the two specified video prompts, formatted per the provided example and modeled on the 'Now: Focus' video style (page text references an example formatting link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Deadline: July 15, 2024
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All materials must be submitted by the stated deadline to be considered.
